convoLines.text: "We gave them a good burial. Doesn't feel like enough, does it? Hm."
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."
You walk to the ridge with Miles. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
"You're kind. Don't let this place change that."
"The whole fire was arguing about Murkcap last night — what to even CALL it. 'The Loud Beast' got shouted down. What's your vote?"
"Take your time."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"I should get back to it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Thanks for... you know. Just listening."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"I don't know what to do with my hands today. How are you holding up, though?"
"Thank you for saying it straight. Most people perform. I'm tired of performances." You feel oddly steadier.
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"We were just talking. Nothing important. Simple as that."
"I work alone. Nothing personal. ...It's a little personal."
You show them Cattail — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Yeah? What's up?"
"Have you heard what they're calling Murkcap? Carolina is pushing 'Big Big'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
They nod. "Okay."
"I'm staying out of the naming fight. For now. Someone always gets precious about their pick."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
"This was good." They mean it.

"We never finished talking about what's been happening — we left it mid-thought, 4 days back. 'A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.' We still owe grief a proper ending, too."
"There's more, but that's for another fire."
"I keep turning over the last thing Silas said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Miles grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Miles is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on what's been happening."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
You show them Greenbrier Shoots — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "I'd follow you out past the treeline. Don't tell the others — they'd want to come too."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"We never finished talking about what's been happening — we got cut off, 4 days back. 'Okay. We'll pick this up later.'"
"Walk with me? I want another pair of eyes on something."
Halfway to the tree line, Elijah freezes. Fresh tracks — big. "We go back now. Quietly." You do. The wild, reminding you.
"Nobody says Silas's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
"I hum one note, over and over, when the dark comes for Silas, now. Feels right. Feels like the least I can do."
"Still on what's been happening."
"I work alone. Nothing personal. ...It's a little personal."
You show them American Ginseng — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "Silas always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good — what's been happening, settled. Feels better said out loud."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Can we talk?" Miles sits down near you. "Just... talk. Like people used to."
"Help me haul something back? Too much for one."
You walk to the cache spot with Miles. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
"We're eating through stores faster than we replace them. Will you forage with me tomorrow? Two pairs of eyes, twice the ground."
"The stores won't stretch past tomorrow, and I'm not choosing who eats. Meet me at the south slope below the meadow and we'll fill packs before dark."
Move next to your partner, on the same side of the Haven door.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "They took you — The Confession, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
«यह कौन सी जगह है? हम कहाँ हैं?» "Water?" — they grin, proud of the one English they know.
They spread their hands, smiling — the words are missing, but the meaning lands anyway.
"Yeah? What's up?"
They answer at length. They nod back, slowly.
They answer at length. They smile back, slower this time, like it just landed.
They answer at length. You tap your chest, then theirs. Us. They nod, emphatic.
You listen hard, watching their mouth shape the words. Sounds, and the shape of meaning just out of reach.
Poulomi laughs — with you, mostly. "Good try! Again — ठीक है।." They walk you through it, patient as sunrise.
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"This was good." They mean it.

deathBeat: d13: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Silas Morozov is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d13: 🕯️ Silas Morozov is dead — the wild. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d13: The village's quarrel was with Silas — and Silas is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d13: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Natalie is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d13: ◈ CRISIS — THE FIRST GRAVE. Natalie is dead. The village digs its first grave, and everyone understands at once: this place can kill you. It just did.
d14: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Nostalgia is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
recoverHome: d14: That night, they bring Silas home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
systemVoice: d13: SYSTEM: "Perimeter violated! This is unprecedented! ...Is this unprecedented? Checking. Yes. Unprecedented."
d13: SYSTEM: "INTRUDER REPELLED. The pantry’s aroma is now classified as a defensive liability. The audience is chanting the defenders’ names. Fan clubs are forming. This is how it starts."

d13: ◈ AUDIENCE TRIAL — SYSTEM: "The audience wants an encore. A trial, then — smaller this time, but televised." Fully identify 3 plants (knowledge level 3) within 3 days. Reward: integration, and a lesson.

d13: ◈ ARC III — ENGINES. SYSTEM: "VIEWERSHIP MILESTONE. Organic unit demonstrates compounding capability. Resonance protocols unlocked." — Your gifts deepen. Used in sequence, they resonate. The village is no longer just surviving. It is becoming something.
d13: SYSTEM: "Oh. Oh no. Was that supposed to happen? The audience is crying. I did not know they could do that."
d14: 📺 SYSTEM: "AUDIENCE EXPANSION! Your party cap is now FOUR! The people demanded bigger ensembles! Don't let us down!"
d14: 📺 SYSTEM: "A viewer sent this. A FAN. We checked. It is not dinner." A pause. "We checked twice. The fans are very insistent that you open it ON CAMERA."
